summary: Social sign-in is a sign-in card with one button per provider, such as Google, GitHub, Figma and SSO, plus a way to continue with email. The provider used last time gets an outline and a Last used badge, so a returning person can find it quickly. After sign-in the card swaps to a welcome message with the provider's name and a Sign out button.
use: When people sign in to your agent product with an existing work account
When returning users tend to forget which provider they used last time
When sign-in calls an OAuth flow that takes a moment and the button should show it is working
When you need a small signed-in confirmation before the product loads
features: Providers show an official `brand` mark, an `icon` such as a lock for SSO, or a `letters` tile.
The `lastUsed` provider gets an outline and a Last used badge, and a successful sign-in updates it.
If `onSignIn` returns a promise, that provider's button spins until it settles and the other buttons wait.
Resolving to false or rejecting keeps the person signed out.
Once signed in, the card shows an avatar, "Welcome back" with the `user` name, which provider was used and a Sign out button.
`title`, `logo` and `emailLabel` change the heading, the mark on the tile and the email link.
a11y: The button that is signing in sets `aria-busy` while its promise is pending.
Every provider is a native button labelled "Continue with" and the provider's name.

faq.q: How do I connect it to my OAuth flow?
faq.a: Handle `onSignIn`, which receives the clicked provider, and return a promise. The button spins until it resolves. Resolve to false or reject to keep the card signed out.

faq.q: How does it remember the last provider between visits?
faq.a: It doesn't store anything itself. Save the key from `onLastUsedChange` wherever you like, then pass it back as `lastUsed` or `defaultLastUsed` next time.

faq.q: Can I add a provider that has no brand mark, like Microsoft?
faq.a: Yes. Give it `letters`, such as "MS", for a letter tile, or an `icon` name. Built-in brand marks cover google, github, figma and slack.
